themes.reason: Sets out the specific quantitative target (30,000 by 2020, 2.3% of workforce) that defines the chosen intervention and anchors the whole proposal; without this the proposal has no concrete shape.
Explains why apprenticeships are the chosen mechanism to address skills shortages, directly linking the intervention to the stated problem of skills gaps.
Explains why apprenticeships are chosen to address the diversity/social mobility part of the problem, forming a second pillar of the rationale alongside skills.
Provides supporting economic justification (productivity, ROI) for the choice but is additional rationale rather than the foundation; the core case rests on skills and diversity goals.
Clarifies that the proposal is not just about numbers but quality, nuancing the intervention design rather than being the central reason for choosing apprenticeships.
Describes the government's role in leading by example, a supporting rationale but not essential to why apprenticeships were chosen to fix skills/diversity problems.
Situates the proposal within wider manifesto and workforce plan commitments; background alignment rather than core justification for the intervention itself.
Reiterates diversity/inclusion aims already captured in the Social Mobility and Diversity theme; supportive but duplicative, not a separate core pillar.
Describes desired apprentice experience, a design detail rather than a reason for choosing the apprenticeship intervention.
Describes intended employment outcomes of apprenticeships, elaborating implementation detail rather than the core rationale.
Miscellaneous procedural and funding details (levy, NAO report) that provide background but do not carry the central argument for the proposal.
